summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump says he has ‘no regrets’ about endorsing Texas Republican Ken Paxton amid leaked recordings – live, Christa Pike severely unwell, ‘angry and confused’, says lawyer, after judge orders all execution evidence preserved – latest, and Trump to speak to Putin about plague lab worker's death in Russia. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are protests, france, and grenades. In the background, Minister denies police brutality as student protests continue across France – Europe live, as it happened and Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump says he has ‘no regrets’ about endorsing Texas Republican Ken Paxton amid leaked recordings – live
headlines.description: The Republican candidate for Texas US Senate was heard complaining at a fundraiser that the Iran war and high gas prices were hurting his campaign In Iowa, we’ll see the Republican nominee for US Senate, Ashley Hinson , face off against Democrat Josh Turek , a state representative and Paralympian at 8pm ET. The race has become one of the most competitive of this cycle, despite the fact a Democrat hasn’t won a Senate election in the Hawkeye state since 2008. Turek, however, trails by just a point in a recent New York Times/Siena College poll. And Hinson, who currently serves as a congresswoman, has pushed back on Donald Trump’s agenda of late, as the president’s approval rating sinks to a new low . Hinson has called for an end on the war in Iran, despite consistently voting against House war powers resolutions that would curb military action, and criticizing the president’s recent pause on tariffs for foreign beef imports, which, Hinson argues, will affect the bottom line for the many cattle ranchers in Iowa.

headlines.title: Christa Pike severely unwell, ‘angry and confused’, says lawyer, after judge orders all execution evidence preserved – latest
headlines.description: Lawyer says Pike cannot move her arms or swallow, has a blot clot and pneumonia, adding that a request to unshackle her was refused; judge tells Tennessee officials to preserve all evidence from botched execution Christa Pike’s lawyers said that Pike remains shackled to her hospital bed. “Based on our understanding, medical staff have asked that the shackles be removed and have been denied that request by [the Tennessee corrections department],” they said, adding: “We would also amend our request and ask for that relief.”

headlines.title: Trump to speak to Putin about plague lab worker's death in Russia
headlines.description: Fears that the death may have been caused by pneumonic plague has prompted calls for more transparency from Russia.

The city mayor, Paweł Niewiadomski, confirmed in a statement that the situation has been contained. “ Henri Kagan discovered a new way of manipulating chemical reactions, allowing a greater excess of one of the mirror images to be created than was previously assumed possible. His discovery has been revolutionary for chemists who develop reactions for the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, flavours, scents and new materials. Kenso Soai designed the first chemical reaction in which only one of the potential mirror images was formed. Other than life itself, no one had ever achieved this feat. The Soai reaction is one of the most spectacular chemical experiments ever conducted.”

headlines.title: Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats
headlines.description: Five children are among the victims of a strike that destroyed 30 flats in northern Ukraine as families slept.

headlines.title: French police suspend use of stun grenades at school protests as minister rejects accusations of brutality
headlines.description: Minister says use of grenades has been stopped after a student lost a hand as protests across France continue How dilapidated are French schools and how bad is inequality in the education system? France’s interior minister has suspended the use of stun grenades by police at high school demonstrations but rejected mounting accusations of police brutality during a fortnight of protests marred by often violent clashes that have injured hundreds. Laurent Nuñez told RTL radio on Wednesday that he had ordered a temporary halt to the use of the grenades “in the context of the high school students’ movement” after a 15-year-old lost a hand during a protest in Lens, northern France, on Monday.

headlinePool.title: Why Trump just loosened the rules on 'dyed diesel' — normally a farm fuel
headlinePool.description: Trump is temporarily allowing this fuel to be used on highways, although it's typically just for off-road farm and construction vehicles. Could that lower the price of diesel?

headlinePool.title: Tories accused of prioritising rich voters as Badenoch lays out inheritance tax cut plan
headlinePool.description: Party hopes to win over affluent middle-class voters as leader rejects calls to ‘unite the right’ in conference speech Kemi Badenoch has announced that the Conservatives would abolish inheritance tax on family homes if elected, prompting criticism that she is prioritising cutting taxes for the rich. The Tory leader also said couples would be able to leave an additional tax-free sum of £1m to their families, as the party attempts to shore up its traditional base in southern England.

headlinePool.title: France halts use of stun grenades after boy's hand blown off in student protests
headlinePool.description: The step comes after several groups complained of police using disproportionate force towards teenagers.

headlinePool.title: British Jewish groups hold London vigil for victims of 7 October attacks
headlinePool.description: Organisations honour those who died three years ago as Andy Burnham says government stands with British Jews British Jewish organisations gathered in central London on Wednesday for a vigil honouring victims of the 7 October attacks in Israel, after a day of tributes from politicians and community leaders. The vigil took place at Richmond Terrace, opposite Downing Street. The Board of Deputies of British Jews said: “Three years ago, Hamas terrorists infiltrated Israel, murdering 1,200 men, women and children, injuring thousands and taking 251 people captive. May their memories for ever remain a blessing.”

headlinePool.title: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
headlinePool.description: People with mental illness alone were to be eligible for assisted dying in Canada in March 2027, but that has now been paused indefinitely.

headlinePool.title: Badenoch’s inheritance tax gambit makes no economic sense | Heather Stewart
headlinePool.description: The Tory leader’s proposal to slash the tax would shovel £6bn of taxpayer money to the already-wealthy Kemi Badenoch’s inheritance tax gambit is a Conservative classic. After all, it was George Osborne’s high-profile pledge to “take the family home out of inheritance tax” in 2007 that put Gordon Brown off calling a snap general election. In practice, Osborne’s plan involved a £1m threshold for inheritance tax – and given the global financial crisis had blown a hole in the public finances by the time the Conservative-Lib Dem coalition came to power in 2010, it never came to pass.

headlinePool.title: The most shocking part of Trump’s comments is what our reaction says about us
headlinePool.description: Listening to the president at a rally these days is a mix of deja vu and word salad, but his decade-long project of division remains abnormal and dangerous This was originally published in This Week in Trumpland. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday Donald Trump’s campaign rallies can be repetitive. Very repetitive. He calls himself the “greatest” president leading the “greatest” movement inside the “greatest” economy. He rails against “Dumocrats” for the “transgender mutilization” of children. He lambasts the “fake news” and reheats election lies. He describes illegal immigration as an “invasion” and recites the poem The Snake. If we were all frogs being slowly boiled alive, we’ve now reached the stage of blackened toad. After a decade of this, presidential utterances that would once have caused outrage are met with a shrug. We are no longer shockable. Or so we thought.

headlinePool.title: Reform clears its own officials of breaking party funding laws despite police investigation
headlinePool.description: Internal inquiry exonerates Dan Jukes and James Orr, who were filmed talking about scheme involving US donor Reform UK has cleared two of its senior officials of breaking laws that ban foreign donations, despite the matter remaining under police investigation. The party published a 27-page report of an internal inquiry finding that Dan Jukes, Nigel Farage’s press adviser, and James Orr, its head of policy, had not breached funding rules.

headlinePool.title: German court orders detention of former intelligence chief after spying arrest
headlinePool.description: August Hanning, 80, appears before judge after being accused of treason and espionage on behalf of foreign state A formal arrest warrant has been issued against Germany’s former top spy, with a judge ordering him to be held in pre-trial detention, a day after he was arrested on suspicion of treason and spying on behalf of an overseas intelligence agency. August Hanning, 80, is accused of buying secret documents from a former colleague and using them to advise a foreign intelligence service, according to the office of the federal prosecutor.
